p: that I made the Children of Israel
אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹמֵר (וַיִּקְרָא כג, מג)
It is brought (in the Gemara, Sukkah 11b)
that there are two opinions in the Gemara:
one says they were the Clouds of Glory,
Now, to understand the meaning of the verse
what is the remembrance of this?
"that I made them dwell in sukkos":
into matzah cakes, for it had not leavened";
and as Rashi of blessed memory explains (there),
that it was a hundred and twenty mil,
and they went it that day in a short time,
and there they made themselves sukkos.
did they make themselves sukkos there?
Did they not know that they would not camp there,
They had only to bake the dough
so that it would not leaven;
but why did they make themselves sukkos?
that even then they made themselves sukkos
according to their halachah, by the Divine word.
And this is "that I made them dwell in sukkos":
And precisely then, at the Exodus from Egypt,
as is known of the special power of the mitzvah of matzah
precisely then they had the mitzvah
As is known, at the Exodus from Egypt
an inner light shone for them
for they then attained a great illumination.
And about this it says there,
"They baked the dough into matzah cakes,"
they tasted with the taste of the mon for thirty days,
הֲגַם שֶׁלֹּא נִצְטַוּוּ אָז עַל מַצָּה
even though they had not then been commanded about matzah,
but only because there then appeared to them
to eliminate the leaven in the dough
by the will of Hashem Yisbarach;
and therefore they tasted in it the taste of the mon.
For on the other days of the year,
it will accomplish nothing in his soul,
as is known from the Tikkunim (Tikkun 36, 77b):
יְהִי אוֹר (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ג) דָּא פֶּסַח
"'Let there be light' (Bereishis 1:3): this is Pesach."
And precisely then they were commanded
in order to reach also the surrounding light,
which is from a high place,
Likewise on the festival of Sukkos,
is the aspect of the surrounding lights,
and through the mitzvah of lulav
as is known from the holy sefarim.
And with this one will understand the derivation
of the gezeirah shavah in the words of Chazal,
"fifteenth, fifteenth" from the festival of Matzos,
where seemingly there is no understanding
of the point of the gezeirah shavah
on the fifteenth day of the month;
what sort of comparison is this?
They also wished to derive the festival of Sukkos
from the festival of Matzos regarding eating matzah,
But according to our words it will be understood
And the command of remembrance will also be settled:
of the mitzvah they were commanded
However, to understand the essence of the matter:
why did He make this mitzvah of sukkah depend
on a remembrance of the mitzvah of the first sukkah
Why is this mitzvah stronger than that one?
וְגַם לְפִי דְּבָרֵינוּ הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל (רְאֵה לְעֵיל מַאֲמָר ז)
And also, according to our words above (see above, maamar 7),
that "so that they may know" means
that the aspect of daas enters
why did He make this depend
on the sukkah of the Exodus from Egypt?
Do we not also now merit
the daas of the surrounding light
This will be understood according to what is known,
and was immediately concealed from them,
because they were not yet then
for they had in their hands
and there was also the claim against them,
Therefore precisely then it was necessary
for the surrounding light to shine upon them
from a very high and exalted place,
also in order to protect them
and to repel from them the external forces,
for they were full of the kelipos
whom they had not yet merited to conquer,
of the impurity of the land of the nations,
וְגַם הַתּוֹרָה עוֹד לֹא נִיתַּן לָהֶם.
and the Torah too had not yet been given to them.
And precisely because there shone upon them
וּכְדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב נב, ב)
And as is brought in the holy Zohar (II 52b)
עַל פָּסוּק מַה תִּצְעַק אֵלָי (שְׁמוֹת יד, טו)
on the verse "Why do you cry out to Me?" (Shemos 14:15):
That is, it was now necessary
to shine upon them from the root,
from the aspect of Atika Kadisha;
that is, the appearance of daas
in the innermost heart from the root,
which is the aspect of Keser in externality,
and it is the aspect of connection with the root,
the connection of the souls of Israel,
as our Sages of blessed memory said
(רַשִׁ"י בְּרֵאשִׁית א, א מִוַּיִּקְרָא רַבָּה לו, ד)
who are called 'the first of His produce'" (Yirmiyahu 2:3);
and through this they were saved,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּמִצְוַת סוּכָּה עַתָּה
This is not so with the mitzvah of sukkah now,
when we have many mitzvos and merits
and there is no need for the surrounding light
daas and feeling in the heart,
even from the surrounding light that was then.
And this is "so that they may know," etc.,
"that I made them dwell in sukkos," etc.,
"when I took them out of the land of Egypt":
that we may merit something of the aspect of the daas
עַל פִּי דְבָרֵינוּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי
according to our words on the second day of Yom Tov
on the allusion of the four species,
the hadas corresponds to the three holy Avos,
וְעַל פִּי הַמִּדְרָשׁ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה ל, יב)
and according to the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 30:12)
it corresponds to those who possess mitzvos,
which is the aspect of Moshe and Aharon,
Netzach and Hod according to the hidden teaching,
who have neither taste nor fragrance,
drew down this power of holiness
"He smelled the fragrance of his garments,"
that is, the sinners of Israel
who are full of mitzvos like a pomegranate.
who were the leaders and providers of the generation,
"You led Your people like a flock
by the hand of Moshe and Aharon,"
וְהִנֵּה כְּבָר דִּבַּרְנוּ (רְאֵה לְעֵיל מַאֲמָר יב)
Now we have already spoken (see above, maamar 12)
of how Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁדִּבַּרְנוּ לְמַעְלָה (רְאֵה לְעֵיל מַאֲמָר א)
and as we spoke above (see above, maamar 1),
when his name was called Yisrael,
and with men, and have prevailed";
and he saw that he could not prevail against him,
and he touched the hollow of his thigh":
the tzaddikim who would come forth from him;
הַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל כָּל פָּנִים עַל זַרְעוֹ
that is, at least concerning his offspring
and then, "for his livestock he made sukkos";
that is, it became clear to him
who are his "livestock" and his acquisitions,
However, this power of his was
only for one who has in him
at least the fragrance of mitzvos,
when receiving the blessings from his father,
"He smelled the fragrance of his traitors,"
who were the groomsmen of the King and the Queen,
to draw down and root the holiness
and to take them out of Egypt,
and to make them "one nation in the land,"
accomplished then, through the mitzvah of sukkah
at the time of the Exodus from Egypt,
to draw down the surrounding light
from a very high and exalted place,
even the empty ones in Israel
גַּם אִם אֵין לָהֶם עַל הַגַּוְון
even if, on the surface, they have
לֹא טַעַם תּוֹרָה וְלֹא רֵיחַ מִצְוֹת.
neither the taste of Torah nor the fragrance of mitzvos.
For such is His conduct, may He be blessed:
that precisely upon a soul that has fallen
from the root in order to raise it up.
Also, the souls of Moshe and Aharon
above the level of the holy Avos,
and Moshe and Aharon in the inner chamber";
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָיָה בָּהֶם כֹּחַ
and through this they had the power
to raise up even the lowest,
And this is the matter of
"In the place where baalei teshuvah stand,
That is, like the teshuvah of
"There is one who acquires his world
nor do they attain the paths of life,"
as our Sages of blessed memory said there,
and when he became embittered over this,
he merited that there shone upon him
from the very high surrounding light,
to connect him to the root of holiness
And something like this was accomplished
to connect every single soul of Israel,
so that through this they are connected,
in the innermost point of their hearts,
And to this the verse alludes:
that I made the Children of Israel
when I took them out of the land of Egypt,"
to allude to our words above.
